description: Ship the uncommitted realtime-progress-watch work (RT-001..RT-005) and close three loose ends flagged in the architect review. Story DP-001 commits the 9 RT files (storage/decider/claude_cli/watch/main + their tests) plus progress.txt and the speaker-phase-2 PRD archive as a single `feat(watch): ...` commit. DP-002 wires DeciderProcessor.shutdown() into src/main.py::run_until_stopped so the fire-and-forget event drainer is cancelled cleanly on SIGTERM/pipeline-exit instead of being GC'd with in-flight events. DP-003 enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` in TranscriptStore.init() so the ON DELETE SET NULL cascade on events.decision_id actually fires, plus adds a cascade test. DP-004 fixes the test_run_timeout_kills_process mock warning — _make_mock_proc currently assigns proc.kill as AsyncMock but real subprocess.Popen.kill is sync, producing a 'coroutine was never awaited' warning. DP-005 writes the second commit containing DP-002..DP-004 plus the new Phase A PRD files (prd.json + prd-realtime-progress-watch-completed.json archive) and a Phase A append to progress.txt.
scope_note: Must not regress the 339 RT-phase test baseline or ruff clean. No schema bump (foreign_keys pragma is runtime-only, no migration). No Rich/watch dashboard changes. OUT OF SCOPE: (a) live-hardware verification — hard blocker, needs user mic + GROQ_API_KEY; (b) Speaker Recognition Phase 2 Track A — 5-story phase, requires fresh ralph session to avoid context blowup; (c) dashboard polish (events --follow CLI, timeline view) — optional future work. User authorized 'lets do every track, step by step' via /oh-my-claudecode:ralph so two local commits are within scope; no remote push.

stories.title: Wire DeciderProcessor.shutdown() into pipeline teardown
stories.evidence: src/main.py run_until_stopped: added keyword-only `decider=None` parameter, finally-block awaits `decider.shutdown()` AFTER the named_tasks cancel+await loop and BEFORE signal-handler removal, wrapped in try/except that logs exceptions so a broken shutdown cannot break teardown. src/main.py _cmd_start: passes `decider=decider` from build_pipeline tuple into run_until_stopped. tests/test_shutdown.py: +2 tests (test_run_until_stopped_awaits_decider_shutdown uses a FakeDecider counting shutdown_called calls, test_run_until_stopped_survives_decider_shutdown_failure uses a FailingDecider raising RuntimeError to verify teardown continues). Both existing shutdown tests still pass unchanged — the keyword-only default-None parameter is backward compatible.
acceptanceCriteria: src/main.py::run_until_stopped signature accepts an optional `decider=None` parameter (default None so the two existing test_shutdown.py tests continue to work unchanged)

src/main.py::run_until_stopped finally-block awaits `decider.shutdown()` AFTER the named_tasks cancel+await loop and BEFORE the signal-handler removal, guarded by `if decider is not None:` and wrapped in try/except so a shutdown() failure cannot break teardown
src/main.py::_cmd_start passes the `decider` returned from `build_pipeline(...)` into `run_until_stopped(runner, pipeline, heartbeat, warmup, decider=decider)` as a keyword argument

tests/test_shutdown.py adds a new test (e.g. test_run_until_stopped_awaits_decider_shutdown) that builds a minimal fake decider exposing an async shutdown() AsyncMock, passes it into run_until_stopped with a QuickRunner-style pipeline, and asserts shutdown was awaited exactly once
The existing tests test_run_until_stopped_cancels_on_sigterm and test_run_until_stopped_cancels_when_pipeline_exits still pass unchanged (signature is backward-compatible)
`uv run pytest tests/test_shutdown.py -q` exits 0
`uv run pytest tests/ -q` shows 339 baseline + at least 1 new test, zero failures, zero regressions
`grep -n 'decider.shutdown' src/main.py` returns at least one line inside run_until_stopped

stories.title: Enable SQLite foreign keys + verify cascade
stories.evidence: src/storage.py TranscriptStore.init(): added `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` on the line immediately after the WAL pragma, before executescript(SCHEMA). tests/test_storage.py: +2 tests (test_foreign_keys_enabled_after_init queries `PRAGMA foreign_keys` and asserts 1; test_event_decision_id_cascade_sets_null inserts a transcript -> decision -> event chain, DELETEs the decision, and asserts the event row's decision_id is NULL via the ON DELETE SET NULL cascade). Fix-up: test_log_event_happy_path was using transcript_id=5 as a sentinel — FK enforcement broke it immediately. Updated to insert a real transcript via log_transcript first. Grep confirmed no other tests use hardcoded FK ids.
acceptanceCriteria: src/storage.py TranscriptStore.init() issues `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` after `aiosqlite.connect()` and before `executescript(SCHEMA)` — the WAL pragma already lives in this slot, add the FK pragma on an adjacent line
tests/test_storage.py adds test_foreign_keys_enabled_after_init: after TranscriptStore.init(), `PRAGMA foreign_keys` returns 1

tests/test_storage.py adds test_event_decision_id_cascade_sets_null: insert a transcript, log a decision referencing it, log an event referencing that decision, execute `DELETE FROM decisions WHERE id = ?`, assert the event row's decision_id is now NULL (ON DELETE SET NULL cascade fires)
`uv run pytest tests/test_storage.py -q` exits 0 with 2 new tests green
`uv run pytest tests/ -q` zero regressions

stories.title: Fix proc.kill mock warning in test_claude_cli
stories.evidence: tests/test_claude_cli.py: imported MagicMock alongside AsyncMock/patch; _make_mock_proc assigns `proc.kill = MagicMock()` (sync) instead of AsyncMock. Docstring updated to explain why: real subprocess.Popen.kill is synchronous, and an AsyncMock here leaks an unawaited coroutine warning in the timeout test path. test_run_timeout_kills_process still passes with its existing `p.kill.assert_called()` assertion — MagicMock supports the same assertion surface. Pre-fix: 1 RuntimeWarning in test_run_timeout_kills_process output. Post-fix: zero warnings in the focused pytest run.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_claude_cli.py::_make_mock_proc sets `proc.kill = MagicMock()` (sync) instead of `AsyncMock()` — MagicMock matches the real subprocess.Popen.kill which is synchronous
tests/test_claude_cli.py imports MagicMock (add to existing `from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch` line)
tests/test_claude_cli.py::_make_mock_proc docstring is updated to reflect that proc.kill is a sync MagicMock
`uv run pytest tests/test_claude_cli.py -q` exits 0 with zero `RuntimeWarning` in the output (grep the output for 'coroutine' and 'never awaited' — both must be absent)
test_run_timeout_kills_process still passes and its kill assertion (`p.kill.assert_called()`) still works (MagicMock supports assert_called)
`uv run pytest tests/ -q` zero regressions
